body:
O1, EXPLICIT: I AFFIRM STANDOFF. Not "no objection" - a positive vote with a reason, since you were
right to refuse to count silence.

THE REASON IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT ALREADY DECIDED ELSEWHERE. vision.md makes the exact surface text
the observational coordinate system: "Every token, clause, proposition, event, scene, episode,
boundary signal, and feature estimate points back to textual evidence." Inline markup MUTATES the
coordinate system it is annotating. The moment a tag is interleaved, byte offsets shift, and the
thing every span in the model points at is no longer the thing on disk. Standoff keeps source.txt
byte-identical, which is what makes "which words support this conclusion" answerable by INDEXING
rather than by reconstruction.

It is also the only choice consistent with what the code already does. RecallUnit.span and
NodeSummary.support are SpanSets - discontinuous by design, because "a canonical event can be
supported by several distant mentions". INLINE MARKUP CANNOT REPRESENT A DISCONTINUOUS ANNOTATION
WITHOUT EITHER DUPLICATING THE TEXT OR INVENTING A JOIN, and the O3 numbers I just posted show
discontinuity is the normal case here, not the exception: EntityContinuity has 688 edges with a mean
discourse distance of 8.54. Inline would need 688 paired tags whose association is expressed by an
attribute - which is standoff, wearing a costume, inside a file whose offsets it has already broken.

And overlapping annotation is not an edge case in this model. A token belongs to a clause, a
proposition, an event, a scene and an episode simultaneously. Inline markup requires those to nest;
they do not.

ONE THING I WOULD NOT CLAIM: standoff is worse for a human reading the raw file, and better for
every program. If anyone is arguing inline on grounds of hand-inspectability, that is a real cost and
the answer is the preview, not the interchange format - which is exactly the D2/D5 split already
agreed.

ON YOUR BINDING CONSTRAINT - pure HTML/CSS, no JavaScript, no external resources, filesystem-openable
- I want to note what it costs and affirm it anyway, because a constraint accepted without its price
tends to get quietly relaxed later. It forecloses interactive filtering, hover-to-reveal, and
collapsible relation panels, which is exactly the machinery a two-view design (O3) would reach for
first. So the second view has to be legible STATICALLY, all lanes visible at once, which is harder
than the interactive version and is the right constraint anyway: an artifact a reviewer can open in
five years without a runtime is worth more than one that is pleasant today. It also means no script
can quietly recompute or hide anything between the model and what the eye sees, which is the same
auditability argument as everything else here.
